tasks.short: Consult a supervisor about family programmes

steps.what: Consult with supervisor about programs for individual families

tasks.design: Keep the consultation between assistant and supervisor. Existing authorised case material in {DOCS} can support the discussion without adding recording or automated family recommendations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supervision depends on family context and professional responsibility.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing case access supports the conversation; no new automation is required.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve conflicting family needs and recognise when further specialist advice is necessary.
tasks.human_edge: Explain uncertainty and challenge an unsuitable programme with the supervisor.
tasks.altitude: Consultation duties and programme decision rights stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Practise concise case formulation and escalation of uncertainty.

evidence.claim: Family supervision is a contextual conversation; automating case-note production does not replace that conversation.

assumptions: Boundary is the assistant's consultation time, excluding separately owned case-note preparation, eligibility decisions and subsequent implementation.
The assistant brings existing family observations and questions; the supervisor produces guidance during s1. No structured suitability or risk flag is assumed.
Supervisor participation remains existing other-role work outside this focal-time denominator and is unchanged.
Use existing authorised case access first. There is no new system, recording or maintenance duty, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Which programme decisions require supervisor authorisation
research_questions: Which uncertainties most often require a second supervisory discussion?

already_counted.description: All assistant consultation and clarification time remains.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, incremental=0, net=0. The discussion remains human even when case material is readily available.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Demonstrate equipment use and care to tenants

steps.what: Demonstrate equipment use and care and coach the tenant's practice

tasks.design: Keep the practical demonstration and tenant practice with the assistant. Refer to the current equipment instructions in {DOCS} where available; no automated assessment of safe use is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: A written instruction does not show whether this tenant can operate this equipment safely.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing instructions remain a reference, with no claimed breakthrough.
tasks.still_hard: Adjust the pace and explanation to the tenant's understanding and physical ability.
tasks.human_edge: Notice hesitation or unsafe handling and demonstrate again.
tasks.altitude: Practical instruction remains part of the assistant's work.

reach.task: Teach safe use of household equipment
reach.learn: Use demonstration and teach-back without assuming comprehension.

evidence.claim: Practical equipment instruction requires observation of the user's actual handling, which a document alone cannot establish.

assumptions: Boundary includes demonstration, tenant practice and corrective instruction; equipment procurement and repair remain separate unchanged work.

The equipment owner provides current manufacturer instructions before s1. The assistant observes tenant practice only after demonstrating during s1; no prior comprehension or safe-use flag is presumed.
Existing tenant participation remains unchanged outside the assistant's focal-time denominator.
Native document access is sufficient. No new tool or record is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero; unavailable instructions require existing manual clarification.
unknowns: Equipment types and restrictions on tenant use
research_questions: Which equipment instructions most often need repeat demonstration?

already_counted.description: Demonstration, observation and corrective coaching remain fully counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and net=0 with no incremental upkeep. Access to instructions does not remove physical demonstration or checking comprehension.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Clarify the tenant's question about sanitation, maintenance or parking rules
Find the current rules established by owner or management
Explain rules and refer ambiguous applications to management

tasks.design: Configure native search and building-specific folders in {DOCS} for current management rules. The assistant selects and reads the source passage, explains it to the tenant and asks management about ambiguous applications.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current rules can be difficult to distinguish from superseded or unrelated building documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document search and version metadata can shorten retrieval without generating an answer.
tasks.still_hard: Explain the rule sensitively and distinguish clarification from granting an exception.
tasks.human_edge: Handle the tenant's circumstances and recognise a question beyond the assistant's authority.
tasks.altitude: Less time finding current passages; no additional enforcement or exception authority.

reach.learn: Read the source passage and check understanding in plain language.

evidence.claim: Native document search can assist source retrieval; the proposed retrieval saving is an unmeasured scenario, not a result from the digest's note-taking cases.

assumptions: Boundary covers clarification, rule lookup and explanation; management writes and approves the underlying rules in its existing separate workflow.

Management supplies each current rule document with building identifier, rule topic, version, effective date and owner. Existing rule-writing time is unchanged; new indexing checks by management are counted as incremental other-role work.

The assistant captures the building context and question during s1 and selects and verifies the actual passage in retained s2 time. Missing metadata or conflicting versions fall back to direct management clarification with no retrieval saving for those cases.
Test native search and version filters before custom code. No generated paraphrase or automated judgement about a tenant is used.

Savings apply only where current manual searching can be shortened, not to existing search runtime. Focal upkeep of 3 hours and management indexing of 2 hours per 100 focal baseline hours are additional.
unknowns: Whether current documents have reliable building and version metadata
research_questions: Does native search reduce passage-finding time without selecting obsolete rules?

already_counted.description: Assistant selects and verifies the rule passage during retrieval.

incremental.description: Check retrieval failures and report stale sources.
Maintain building and version indexing beyond existing rule authorship.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=20+30*0.75+50=92.5; gross=7.5, focal upkeep=3, central net=4.5. A conservative 0-2.5 range allows poor indexing and frequent clarification; tenant conversation receives no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe food selections and suggest economical nutritious alternatives

steps.what: Observe clients' food selections and recommend economical and nutritional alternatives

tasks.design: Keep observation and discussion of alternatives with the assistant. Existing general nutrition guidance in {DOCS} can support the conversation, while specialist dietary questions go to the appropriate professional.
tasks.previous_blocker: Affordable food choices depend on actual availability, preferences and the client's situation.
tasks.enabler_now: Reference access does not remove the observation and supportive discussion.
tasks.still_hard: Balance affordability, practical cooking options and nutrition without assuming undisclosed dietary restrictions.
tasks.human_edge: Discuss realistic alternatives without shaming the client.
tasks.altitude: The assistant continues to support choices within existing competence.

reach.learn: Recognise when dietary questions need specialist advice.

evidence.claim: Supportive discussion of actual food choices remains contextual human work; generic guidance does not establish individual dietary suitability.

assumptions: Boundary is observation and supportive recommendations, excluding budget preparation, purchasing and specialist dietary assessment.

The client makes the food selections before observation; the assistant gathers preferences and checks displayed prices during s1. No structured dietary suitability, allergy or affordability flag is presumed.

General reference guidance is maintained by its existing owner; this unchanged design adds no tool, recording or upkeep. Native document access is sufficient and unclear cases use existing professional referral.
unknowns: Assistant's permitted scope for nutrition advice
Clients' access to cooking and food storage
research_questions: Which barriers prevent clients from using the suggested alternatives?

already_counted.description: Observation and discussion remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new system or ongoing duty.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Observing actual food choices and discussing feasible alternatives remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The assistant still provides direct support and seeks supervision; rule retrieval becomes modestly quicker where indexing is reliable.
reach: Explain service requirements with community health workers.
Bring clear questions to family social workers.
role.ambitious_version: Provide clear, contextual support without delegating family or dietary judgements to software.
